newsitem.title: UK: UK radio authority opposes DMG acquisition.
newsitem.headline: UK radio authority opposes DMG acquisition.

text.p: Britain's Radio Authority ruled on Monday that the proposed acquisition of the Leicester Sound station by DMG Radio was against the public interest.
Leicester Sound would lose its licence if the proposed acquisition went ahead, the radio watchdog said after conducting its first cross-media public interest test.
DMG Radio is a subsidiary of Daily Mail and General Trust Plc.

Daily Mail and General Trust owns Associated Newspapers, which publishes The Daily Mail and The Mail on Sunday, plus local newspaper group Northcliffe, whose titles include the Leicester Mercury and several freesheets in the Leicester area.
The Radio Authority said that the acqusition could lead to a reduction in diversity in the sources of information available to the public in the Leicester area.
DMG Radio agreed last August to buy an 80 percent stake in Leicester Sound from GWR Group Plc.

This was the first occasion on which the Radio Authority had considered acquisitions between newspaper groups and licence holders in the light of the new cross-media public interest test provisions introduced by the 1996 Broadcasting Act.
